speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision. To begin my assessment, can you describe exactly how the leg was positioned when you were first found, and is the pain sharp or a dull ache?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Femoral Neck Fracture.

Thank you for the details; the mechanism of injury (rear-end collision) combined with immediate severe groin pain and abnormal leg positioning is highly suggestive of a femoral neck fracture. Before we finalize this, do you currently have any ability to bear weight on the right leg at all?
